subject: POC: Prompt & Eval Dataset — next steps and success criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@acmehealth.com>, Priya Kumar <priya.kumar@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Mar 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: POC: Prompt & Eval Dataset — next steps and success criteria

Hi Sam and Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great discussion. As promised, here’s a concise recap and proposed plan to move the POC forward so we can validate fit quickly: 

1) Success criteria (what success looks like for Acme Health):
- Precision baseline: >= 85% on clinical note extraction tasks (per your internal eval set)
- Latency: 95th percentile generation time < 250ms for single-turn prompts at your expected concurrency
- Cost target: per-request token cost that keeps average monthly inference spend within the $X–Yk target (we'll produce estimates once we have sample volumes)

2) Eval dataset & prompts we need from your side (priority order):
- eval_prompt_list.csv (single-line prompts + expected output examples) — this will be used for the prompt/eval harness
- 2–3 weeks of anonymized assistant logs (logs sample) for distribution/edge-case coverage — acme_logs_sample.zip
- A short set of 20–30 high-priority prompts you want the POC to demonstrate on day 1

3) Timeline (draft):
- By Apr 2: Acme provides eval_prompt_list.csv + sample logs + 20–30 priority prompts
- Apr 3–7: Redwood prepares eval harness, ingests prompts, and runs baseline evals on recommended model variants
- Apr 8: Joint review call to go over baseline results, adjust success criteria, and finalize test plan
- Apr 9–16: POC runs with instrumentation (latency/cost/quality), daily syncs optional

4) Ownership / contacts:
- Acme: Sam (product lead) / Priya (data lead) — provide prompts & logs, confirm clinical anonymization
- Redwood: Marissa (CS lead) — POC PM; Aditya (AE) — commercial lead; Dev (SE) — technical integration and eval harness

5) Next steps for this week:
- Sam/Priya: confirm they can send the requested files by EOD Apr 2 and whether the logs need an NDA addendum
- Redwood: I'll share the eval template (CSV) and a sample runbook; Dev will draft the POC runbook and baseline model suggestions

Attachments: eval_prompt_list.csv (template) and initial_sow_draft.pdf (POC scope/assumptions) referenced.

If that matches your expectations, I’ll follow up with the CSV template and a calendar invite for the Apr 8 review.

Best,
Marissa
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 415-555-0123

From: Sam Turner <sam.turner@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Kumar <priya.kumar@acmehealth.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC: Prompt & Eval Dataset — next steps and success criteria

Thanks Marissa — this looks good and aligns with what we discussed. Quick answers: 

- We can provide the eval_prompt_list.csv and the 20–30 priority prompts by EOD Apr 2.
- Logs: we can share a 1-week anonymized logs sample now (we’ll scrub PHI fields). If you need more, we can do 3 weeks but likely will need a DPA/processing addendum signed first.

I attached a small sample (acme_logs_sample.zip) with obfuscated IDs — please confirm the format is usable. Also attaching a short doc with our expected throughput and concurrency estimates.

One question on the success criteria: the 85% precision target is OK for many of our extraction tasks, but for a specific clinical entity (medication dosing) we might need an 90% bar. Can we flag that as a high-priority basket of prompts for the POC?

Sam
Product Lead, Acme Health
sam.turner@acmehealth.com

Attachments: acme_logs_sample.zip

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC: Prompt & Eval Dataset — next steps and success criteria

Sam — perfect, thanks for the quick turnaround and for flagging medication dosing as a higher bar. We’ll: 

- Mark medication-dosing prompts as priority-1 with a separate success threshold (>= 90% precision). Please include those in the 20–30 priority prompts if possible.
- Dev: I’ve asked you to confirm the logs format — can you confirm we can ingest the attached sample as-is and whether you need additional fields?

Aditya — do you want to confirm the commercial side (any limits on trial size or data retention notes) so Sam has visibility?

I’ll upload the template and a concise runbook to the shared Drive folder and send the calendar invite for Apr 8 review after we confirm the sample ingestion.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Sam Turner <sam.turner@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2026 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC: Prompt & Eval Dataset — next steps and success criteria

Thanks — looked through acme_logs_sample.zip quickly. Format looks fine (CSV of events with timestamp, obfuscated_patient_id, prompt_text, assistant_response). A couple of notes: 

- Please include a short schema file (CSV or JSON schema) that lists column names and an example row — makes ingestion much faster.
- For the anonymization: removing direct PHI is good, but keep event timestamps and relative ordering — that helps with temporal failure modes.
- We can ingest the sample as-is and run a baseline on the model variants I’ll propose. I’ll upload a short README to the Drive folder with exact ingestion steps and the eval harness command.

Marissa/Aditya: I’ll aim to have the baseline results (initial model choices and a short runbook) by Apr 7 so we can review on Apr 8.

-Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwoodinference.com
